title: Cohere: Building enterprise LLM agents that work (Shaan Desai)
talk_summary: Cohere's ML engineer argues enterprise agents should start with a single LLM and a few well-specified tools, use constrained multi-agent routing only when needed, and codify human-in-the-loop triggers. He emphasizes golden-set evaluation of intermediate tool calls/parameters plus a failure-mitigation ladder from prompt/tool-spec fixes to targeted annotation and synthetic-data fine-tuning.

takeaways.what_they_do: They build a ground-truth corpus with expected tool calls, parameter inputs, outputs, and final responses, then run it through the agent framework to locate failure points.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we build a golden set of ground truuth user queries expected function calls expected parameter inputs expected outputs

takeaways.technique: Retrieve/cache history instead of long transcripts
takeaways.what_they_do: They warn that long chat histories can induce hallucinations and recommend caching history and retrieving only what is relevant to the new query.
takeaways.evidence_quote: long streams of chat history in other words back and forth conversations between the user and chatbot that go over 20 turns for example can induce certain hallucinations

takeaways.what_they_do: They simplify tool descriptions, add sharp call examples, flatten complex nested inputs into simple types, and keep instruction lists short.
takeaways.evidence_quote: clear descriptions with very sharp examples on how to call the tool as well as providing and simplifying the input type

takeaways.what_they_do: They give the router clear tools and routing instructions including edge cases, and constrain subagents to independent tasks with small tool sets.
takeaways.evidence_quote: sub agent they should be constrainted to performing independent tasks with a small set of tools

takeaways.what_they_do: They codify rules that force human approval before or after risky tool calls, such as sending emails or processing sensitive outputs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can codify a set of rules under which human in the loop is triggered

takeaways.what_they_do: They use prompt/tool-spec fixes for low failure rates, targeted annotation datasets for 10-20% failures, and synthetic-data fine-tuning for high failure rates.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you do see a tool type failure or model hallucinate on specific uh task uh in the 10 to 20% range
